title: fix(telegram): retry preview edits after transient server errors
body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Telegram returned a transient server error (HTTP 502 or 503) for one edit of a streaming preview, OpenClaw gave up on that preview message and sent the answer as a second message. The chat was left with a stale, half-finished preview plus a duplicate final reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.ts` classified which failures are safe to retry. Server errors were excluded even though editing an existing message is idempotent (the classification was added in `ff04e24eade` on top of the in-place transport from `a69e82765f2`). Transient 5xx responses on preview edits are now retried like other transient failures. The first send stays protected against duplicate delivery, so only idempotent edits are retried.

## User Impact

A brief Telegram outage during streaming now ends with one message containing the complete answer, instead of an abandoned preview plus a duplicate.

## Evidence

- New regressions reject a single preview edit with 502 and with 503. Before the fix there were two sends; after, one original message carries the completed answer. All 23 Telegram HTTP tests pass. A follow-up test-only commit removes a redundant assertion.
- Lane proof on Blacksmith Testboxes: 874 tests across 39 adapter suites, 17 isolated Gateway E2E cases, full build, and `check-changed`.
- Production +3/-3; tests +29.
